claims.text: Greg Short describes surrounding himself with young people who are on top of digital trends as his single biggest growth hack, because the new generation understands and adopts emerging digital platforms (e.g., TikTok) faster than established founders do, giving the founder access to platform knowledge he cannot acquire fast enough on his own.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Founder is not personally fluent in current digital platforms
Context: content or digital marketing growth
claims.mechanism: Young people adopt and master new digital platforms faster than established founders; hiring them transfers that platform knowledge into the business without requiring the founder to learn each platform personally.
bounded_by: Speaker applies this to digital marketing platforms specifically (TikTok cited); applicability to non-digital or offline channels is unstated

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that winning at digital marketing is achievable even when the founder personally does not understand the newest platform tactics, provided the execution team is young and trend-aware.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Execution team is young and embedded in current digital trends
Founder is willing to delegate platform execution fully to the team
bounded_by: No evidence cited beyond speaker's own experience; no cohort data or comparison group provided

examples.text: Greg Short is personally still learning TikTok and has a very young team handling the platform on his behalf. He observes that in Miami he sees increasingly younger people adopting digital business opportunities each year, which reinforces his practice of surrounding himself with that cohort as a source of platform and trend knowledge.

practices.text: Surround yourself with young people who are actively using and experimenting with the newest digital platforms; they are the fastest source of practical knowledge on emerging trends.
